flag_note: Effects Database documents both Fi-Sonic Fuzz-Blender and Fuzz-Blender MkIV. The earliest surviving documentary evidence now points to a plain Fuzz-Blender in 1965-1967, while the MkIV is a later distinct physical state. Keep both inside one Fi-Sonic lineage and do not invent undocumented MkII/MkIII models.

Australian period advertisements found by Tone Machines Blog document Fi-Sonic fuzz products in September and December 1965. Exact specimen matching between those advertisements and the surviving plain Fuzz-Blender remains unresolved, so the 1965 date is retained as documentary evidence rather than a hard production-start claim.

OzValveAmps records a surviving Fi-Sonic Fuzz-Blender MkIV and reports that Phil Dreoni confirmed it was one of his creations. This directly anchors the pedal to the Fi-Sonic builder identity and prevents misclassification as an anonymous Australian fuzz.

The MkIV is known, and a separate plain Fuzz-Blender survives, but no reliable documentary evidence currently establishes MkII or MkIII. Keep these names in a discovery queue only; do not create catalog records without evidence.
